subject: Post-call: Concurrency & streaming SLOs — Catalyst Health pilot
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@catalysthealth.com>; Priya Shah <priya.shah@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Concurrency & streaming SLOs — Catalyst Health pilot

Thanks again for the call earlier today — good conversation. Recap and proposed next steps below so we have an aligned starting point for the pilot.

Key takeaways from today's discovery:
- Pilot scope: 6-week production-like pilot behind Catalyst Health's staging environment.
- Workload types: (A) short completions (single-turn patient triage responses), (B) streaming transcripts for live support (token stream to client).
- Performance targets discussed: target P95 latency for completions <= 500ms, streaming tail P95 per-token latency <= 250ms, and overall 99th percentile fallbacks to our cheaper model if hot paths spike.

Catalyst-provided estimates (Alex/Priya):
- Sustained request rate: ~120 req/s (short completions)
- Concurrency (simultaneous open streams): average ~200, peak ~400 during morning surge
- Burst behavior: expected short bursts to 600+ req/s for ~2–5 minutes during campaign launches
- Typical completion sizes: 30–80 tokens; streaming average token rate ~30 tokens/s per session

What we need from Redwood (action items):
1) Redwood to propose a concurrency/connection-pool and rate-limit plan that meets the peak/burst profile while keeping cost predictable. Include recommended reserved capacity vs. burst allowances.
2) Clarify streaming session limits (max concurrent streams per customer + per-region limits).
3) Provide an initial rate card/credit estimate and any short-term pilot accommodations (trial credits, warm-up burst allowances).
4) Attach any runbook/ops requirements we need on Catalyst side (IP whitelists, certs, keepalive expectations).

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Redwood to provide a formal quota proposal and a short workbook we can use to stress-test numbers (due EOD Thu PDT).
- Catalyst to confirm exact spike windows and provide a small sample trace to validate per-token rates.

Thanks — I'll loop Ben and Marissa on the quota proposal.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: conn_quota_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@catalysthealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@catalysthealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Concurrency & streaming SLOs — Catalyst Health pilot

Thanks Vanessa — quick clarifications from our side:

- The 200 avg concurrent open stream sessions I mentioned are "active" bi-directional websockets where clients are receiving tokens continuously. Peak active streams hit ~300 in our busiest clinics. Apologies for the earlier conflation of sessions vs. request concurrency.
- For short completions: 120 req/s sustained is accurate; simultaneous short-completion concurrency tends to align with active user load and can spike to ~650 req/s during promotional emails. Spikes last between 90s–5m depending on campaign cadence.
- When we said "burst to 600 req/s" that combined both streaming and short-completion requests; to be safe, assume bursts can push total token-generation QPS equivalent to ~800 small-completions for 2–3 minutes.

Non-functional constraints:
- Regulatory: all logs must be retained for 90 days with ability to redact PHI before any handoff. We'll follow up with a formal security questionnaire but wanted to flag retention window now.
- Network: we prefer long-lived connections (keepalive = 60s) to avoid connection churn.

What helps us evaluate: a concrete proposal that maps: reserved concurrency, burst buffer length, per-second token/QPS caps, and fallbacks (which model, and whether the fallback is automatic or controlled by request header).

If you can also call out what we should expect for warm-up behavior (first-hour tail latency) that would be useful.

—Alex Ramos
Director, Platform Engineering
Catalyst Health

On Wed, May 12, 2027 at 08:30 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex/Priya — quick note, we'll incorporate these clarifications into the quota workbook and proposal.
>

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@catalysthealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-13T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood pilot quota proposal — initial offer

Alex / Priya / Vanessa — thanks for the details. Attached is our initial proposal (redwood_conn_quota_proposal.pdf) and a companion workbook (conn_quota_workbook.xlsx) with editable fields — copying the key items here so it's easy to comment.

Summary of proposal (pilot-specific):
- Reserved concurrency (streams): 300 concurrent streaming sessions reserved in us-east region.
- Connection pool recommendation: allow up to 350 simultaneous TCP+TLS connections for Catalyst's staging cluster to avoid head-of-line exhaustion when sessions shift between nodes.
- Short-completion throughput: reserved 200 sustained req/s per endpoint, with burst credit to 800 req/s for up to 3 minutes. Bursts are metered from a 90s rolling token bucket; sustained usage above reservation is billed at an overage rate.
- Per-token latency SLOs: target P95 <= 500ms for short completions; streaming per-token P95 <= 250ms. We commit to autoscaling targets to maintain these under the reserved footprint; extended spikes may route to a slightly smaller compatible model (fallback) which we will list in the proposal.
- Warm-up expectations: expect 10–15 minutes of elevated tail latency in the first hour after significant scale increases (we recommend a 30-minute warm-up window for the first production-day run).

Pilot commercial terms (estimates for discussion):
- Pilot waived for first 30 days beyond a one-time setup fee of $5k (covers dedicated capacity reservations and runbook integration).
- Reserve pricing SKU: monthly reservation equivalent during pilot price is pro-rated; overage rates and burst credit pricing are detailed in the attached PDF.
- We can provide one-time short-term burst credit (covering up to 600k tokens) for campaign testing during the pilot.

Operational notes and asks for Catalyst:
- IP ranges to whitelist (we've added a Drive link with the full list).
- Keepalive and idle timeout settings we recommend (keepalive 60s, idle TTL 10m).
- A small sample trace (JSON) illustrating token rates per session would help us validate the workbook assumptions.

Next steps:
1) Vanessa to gather final confirmation from Catalyst on peak burst windows and decide whether to accept the 300 reserved streams or request 350.
2) Catalyst to confirm signature on an MSA addendum for pilot terms (we can prefill language).
3) Redwood to provision capacity upon signed addendum and schedule a joint smoke test (target: week of 2027-05-24).

If the team prefers, we can also offer a staged increase (200 -> 300 -> 350) to keep cost upfront lower and validate real traffic before scaling.

—Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_conn_quota_proposal.pdf (proposal), conn_quota_workbook.xlsx (editable workbook)

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@catalysthealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@catalysthealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot quota proposal — initial offer

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear breakdown and the workbook. Quick responses from Catalyst side:

- We can accept the 300 reserved streaming sessions to start. We'd like the option to request a one-time short-term bump to 400 for the go-live smoke test window (we'll highlight the exact 30-minute window once we have the schedule).
- We accept the burst model as outlined; please confirm the exact overage rate for QPS above reservation so finance can sign off.
- Please include the fallback model names in writing (automatic fallback vs. opt-in header control) — we prefer to opt into fallback behavior during the pilot rather than automatic switching.
- On logs/retention: we'll begin the SOC/security questionnaire but confirm you can retain telemetry for 90 days and redact PHI on request.

Action items we will take this week:
- Share sample token traces (Alex) by Thu EOD.
- Legal to review the MSA addendum — Vanessa will send the prefilled doc.

If Redwood can confirm the one-time warm-up behavior and an exact overage price per 1k tokens, we can get the finance/meetings scheduled and turn the pilot on.

—Priya Shah
Head of Product Operations, Catalyst Health
priya.shah@catalysthealth.com
